candidates.reason: The key binding authority on consideration for contract variations is Williams v Roffey Bros (J32), which allows a promise of extra payment when a practical benefit is obtained, distinguishing it from Stilk v Myrick (J31) which represents the older rule that performing an existing duty is not good consideration. High Trees (J33) is relevant for promissory estoppel as a potential alternative basis. Balfour v Balfour (J29) and Carlill v Carbolic Smoke Ball Co (J23) are less directly relevant but provide context on legal relations and offer principles.

liquidated damages effect on contract variation enforceability
candidates.reason: Dunlop Pneumatic Tyre Co Ltd v New Garage (J48) is the prime authority on liquidated damages clauses and their enforceability, helping understand the impact on related contractual promises. Photo Production v Securicor (J44) on interpretation of contract clauses and risk allocation is also relevant. Entores v Miles Far East (J28) and Hadley v Baxendale (J34) provide principles on contract formation and damages which may be indirectly pertinent. Hochster v De La Tour (J46) on anticipatory breach may offer insight on related breach and enforcement issues.
